newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia energy market should not copy UK-Incitec.
newsitem.headline: Australia energy market should not copy UK-Incitec.

text.p: Australia's newly-deregulated electricity markets should look to Scandinavia and California as the right models for the industry rather than the U.K., Incitec Ltd supply manager, Jim McLeod said on Wednesday.
"North America, particularly Canada, (also) provides a role model for energy regulation," McLeod said in an speech presented to a Queensland power conference.

The Scandinavian electricity market and upcoming Californian market allowed direct contracting independent of an electricity pool "which works well and is the right model for Australia, not the England/Wales model," McLeod said.
There was now growing opinion, particularly among electricity users and their regulator in England and Wales, that there were some serious problems with the way the pool operated there, McLeod said.
"In England/Wales, after seven years of operation, the pool is regarded by industrial users as a technical success and a commercial failure," he said.

McLeod said it was generally agreed that in Australia, regulation of inter and intra-state transmission of gas and electricity would eventually move to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).

"I believe that only the ACCC can resist the strong political influence of large state-based monopolies," McLeod said. Incitec, a fertiliser and chemicals producer, is majority owned by ICI Australia Ltd.
